17 A box of weight 40 N is pushed with a horizontal force of 20 N along level ground for a distance of
2.4 m.
The box is then lifted at constant velocity through a height of 1.6 m by a vertical force.
What is the total work done on the box by the two forces?
A
80 J
B
110 J
C
120 J
D
160 J

hints: Notice the two separate stages: a 20 N horizontal push over 2.4 m, then a vertical lift of 1.6 m at constant velocity.
Recall that work done is $W = Fd$ when force and displacement are parallel, and that constant velocity lifting means the upward force must balance the 40 N weight.
Calculate the horizontal work and the vertical work separately in joules, add them, then round to match the 2 significant figure options.
walkthrough: Identify the horizontal stage: force $F = 20 \text{ N}$ parallel to displacement $d = 2.4 \text{ m}$, so $W_{horizontal} = Fd$.
Identify the vertical stage: lifted at constant velocity, so resultant force is zero and the upward lifting force equals the weight, $F = 40 \text{ N}$, over $d = 1.6 \text{ m}$.
Substitute values with units: $W_{horizontal} = 20 \times 2.4 = 48 \text{ J}$ and $W_{vertical} = 40 \times 1.6 = 64 \text{ J}$.
Compare with the options given to 2 significant figures: $112 \text{ J}$ is given as $110 \text{ J}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: 80 J does not equal the sum of $20 \text{ N} \times 2.4 \text{ m}$ and $40 \text{ N} \times 1.6 \text{ m}$.

B.explanation: Horizontal work $48 \text{ J}$ plus vertical work $64 \text{ J}$ gives $112 \text{ J}$, which to 2 significant figures is $110 \text{ J}$.

C.explanation: 120 J is too large and does not follow from $48 \text{ J} + 64 \text{ J}$ for the 2.4 m push and 1.6 m lift.

D.explanation: 160 J is the result of incorrectly using the 40 N weight for both distances as $40 \times (2.4 + 1.6)$.
